key_insight: A reasoning-capable LLM can substantially improve speaker recognition in long TV dramas by using storyline context to resolve who is speaking. The paper also introduces a large-scale benchmark, DramaSR-532K, to make this problem measurable and trainable at scale.
problem_solved: The paper addresses speaker recognition in long-form TV dramas, where attributing each utterance to the correct character is difficult because of many characters, long-range context, and complex storylines.
method: Builds DramaSR-532K, a large benchmark with 532K annotated dialogue lines and 900+ characters.
Uses a reasoning LLM to incorporate narrative context and speaker-related cues beyond local utterance text.
Evaluates speaker attribution in challenging long-form drama settings to improve comprehensive video understanding.
impact: This work gives AI/ML practitioners a stronger benchmark and a more capable reasoning-based approach for dialogue attribution in videos. It is especially useful for applications like video analysis, character tracking, and story understanding.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing dialogue lines flowing into a reasoning LLM and outputting speaker labels
Benchmark infographic with 532K dialogue lines and 900+ characters highlighted
Storyline timeline visual illustrating long-range context across scenes
Accuracy comparison chart between baseline models and the reasoning LLM
paper_title: Reasoning LLM Improves Speaker Recognition in Long-form TV Dramas
paper_authors: Yuxuan Li, Lingxi Xie, Xinyue Huo, Jihao Qiu, Jiacheng Shao
